# vphone-cli Run a virtual iPhone on an Apple Silicon Mac. > [!WARNING] > This project has never issued or authorized any cryptocurrency or token, and does not accept cryptocurrency payments or donations. Any cryptocurrency or token issued or promoted in this project's name, or claiming any affiliation with it, is a scam. vphone-cli runs iOS with Apple's Virtualization.framework and PCC research virtual machines, for security research, reverse engineering, and debugging. ## Documentation Everything else lives on the documentation site: **** - [Quick Start](https://lakr233.github.io/vphone-cli/get-started/quick-start): requirements, host settings, and your first VM with Launchpad. - [Manual](https://lakr233.github.io/vphone-cli/get-started/overview): machines, firmware, storage, networking, and troubleshooting, in English, 中文, 日本語 and 한국어. - [Research Notes](https://lakr233.github.io/vphone-cli/research/): patches, boot chain, restore, and the automation API reference. The sources of the site are in [`Documents/`](Documents/) and [`Research/`](Research/). ## Let an Agent Install It If you use a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, or similar) on this Mac, paste the prompt below instead of following the steps by hand. The agent reads the vphone skill, checks what is already set up, installs Launchpad and `VPhone.bundle`, and stops to ask when a step needs you, such as an administrator password or a change in macOS Recovery. ```text Set up vphone on this Mac. Read the skill at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/main/Skills/vphone-guest-control/SKILL.md and the files it links under references/ (same folder), then follow them: install the newest notarized vphone-launchpad (not every release has a -notarized zip), put vphone-launchpad-cli on PATH, install the VPhone.bundle that matches Launchpad's series, and check `vphone-launchpad-cli status`. Do not change SIP, boot-args or any other host security setting, and do not create a machine until I confirm the firmware and the free disk space. When a step needs me, tell me exactly what to do and wait. ``` ## Acknowledgements - [wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup](https://github.com/wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup) - [owngoal-dev/OpenAVB](https://github.com/owngoal-dev/OpenAVB) and [owngoal-dev/OpenSEP](https://github.com/owngoal-dev/OpenSEP), the boot ROMs new VMs start from ## License vphone-cli is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

releases.name: vphone 2.16.0
releases.body:
## vphone 2.16.0

**Core Bundle**

- Apple Vision Pro (experimental): visionOS 26.4 (23O247) on the cloudOS 26.4 boot chain with a `visionos` preset: a headless baseline with application management through the iPad compatibility environment and Irisin rootless bootstrap. Native UI, environments and 60 Hz pacing are separate opt-in patches. visionOS is not in `fw catalog`; create it from the IPSW with `--device RealityDevice14,1`. `vm create` builds it without a template, as Launchpad does. (#847, #860, #880)
- iPhone Duo on iOS 27.2: offered in the catalog; WebDriverAgent gets the hinge angle after boot and when started later, and VirtualAudio works on 27.2. (#826, #832)
- iPhone 16 on iOS 18.6.2 (cloudOS 26.1): `fw patch` no longer stops on the cloudOS 26.1 to 26.3 TXM, the EXC_GUARD patch finds `thread_guard_violation` on 26.x kernels, and the guest gets a GPU from the cloudOS 18.6 driver. (#822, #829, #863)
- DriverKit for virtual USB touch input on iPhone and iPad, including a `cfw patch-dt-driverkit` repair for existing machines. (#867)
- Xcode and Instruments: `vm config --developer-tunnel on` keeps a guest's CoreDevice tunnel open so it is listed online, and Time Profiler sy

releases.name: vphone 2.15.2
releases.body:
## vphone 2.15.2

A localization and documentation release. Nothing changes in how Launchpad and `VPhone.bundle` work together.

**Core Bundle**

- Japanese, Korean and Vietnamese have no missing strings in the VM window, its menus and panels (149 strings each, including the HomePod, HomeView, foldable and Apple TV remote controls).
- Simplified Chinese reviewed in full: consistent terms (App, 存储, 虚拟机, 客户机, 宗卷), Apple's own wording, and the missing strings filled in.
- Four strings that meant two things now translate separately: the foldable "Open" posture, the UDID alert's "Set" button, the keyboard panel's "Type" button, and the kernelcache caption in New Machine. English text is unchanged.
- `vm config --help` and the `--ip` error name the network nat machines use by default, 192.168.65.0/24 (192.168.64.0/24 with `--nat-peers off`).

**Launchpad 2.15.2**

- Same translation work for Launchpad's own strings.
- `vphone-launchpad-2.15.2.zip` is built by CI and not notarized; macOS blocks it the first time you open it (see [Downloads](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/blob/main/Documents/Downloads/README.md)). A notarized build follows.

releases.name: vphone 2.15.1
releases.body:
## vphone 2.15.1

**Core Bundle**

- Minimal and watchos keep their iBEC and LLB patches. #806, merged after 2.15.0, dropped them, and Apple's LLB does not start on a VM with 4096 MB or less, so this never shipped. AVPBooter and iBSS stay stock. (#813)
- `device.info` answers right away on tvOS and HomePod guests. Each call used to ask amfid for the Developer Mode state, and amfid there never answers, so every call waited ten seconds and clients with a shorter timeout reported vphoned as unreachable. vphoned now reads Developer Mode in the background and `device.info` returns the cached state. (#814)
- Userspace debugging as a feature: one box in Launchpad's Patches sheet (or `--allow` for its patches) lets debugserver attach to any guest process on `minimal`, watchOS and HomePod guests, with the rest of the preset unchanged. (#810)
- `standard` works on iOS 18.x guests on their own release's cloudOS (checked on iOS 18.6, with debugserver and Frida). 26.x and 27.x guests get the same bytes as before. (#808)
- Minimal: the regenerated static trust cache carries Apple's launch-constraint categories, and the edited `launchd.plist` is signed so a stock `launchd_cache_loader` accepts it

releases.name: vphone 2.15.0
releases.body:
## vphone 2.15.0

**Core Bundle**

- HomeView guests (HomeAccessory17,1 and 17,2, J490/J491): firmware preparation, a `homeview` preset, USB touch input and an optional, reversible setup bypass. Scoped sandbox lookups that blocked BreadBoard and guest-profile initialization are fixed. Display geometry is still provisional. (#786)
- OpenGL ES renders in guests: `EAGLContext` returns contexts for APIs 1–3 and GL draws reach the screen. The kernel names the GLES renderer (`kernel-cfw-paravirt_gles_renderer`), the guest compiler plugin completes the AIR modules OpenGL ES sends, and the paravirtual GPU driver no longer sends primitive restart (`system-paravirt_gpu-cfw-primitive_restart`). Both patches are on in `standard` and blocked by the tvOS and HomePod presets. `cfw update-environment` now also replaces an installed guest's compiler plugin when the bundle's copy differs. (#798)
- iPhone Duo with WebDriverAgent: the inner display is published to every process at point scale 3 and as a built-in panel (type 0), so WDA lists it with the right size and its inner screenshot fills the frame, and `display.modes` reports scale 3 and type 0. releases.name: vphone 2.14.2
releases.body:
## vphone 2.14.2

**Core Bundle**

- Clicks reach the guest again in a VM window larger than 100%. Since 2.14.0 the window measured clicks against the panel at its 100% size, so in an enlarged window (resized, or restored from a saved frame) clicks landed off target or were clamped to the edge and sent as edge swipes. This showed up as dead clicks after resizing an Apple Watch window and after folding an iPhone Duo whose window was enlarged. Folding itself never broke touch in the guest. (#785)

**Launchpad 2.14.2**

- No source changes besides the version. No argument or output Launchpad uses, bundle layout, receipt or escalator changed, so the 2.14 series stays interchangeable both ways and the minimum bundle stays 2.14.0. The helper is unchanged (build 21).
- `vphone-launchpad-2.14.2.zip` is built by CI and not notarized; macOS blocks it the first time you open it (see [Downloads](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/blob/main/Documents/Downloads/README.md)). `vphone-launchpad-2.14.0-notarized.zip` keeps working with this bundle.

**Upgrading**

In Launchpad's Core Bundle page, install `VPhone.bundle` 2.14.2 and bind your machines to it. The fix is in the VM window on the host;

vphone-cli

Run a virtual iPhone on an Apple Silicon Mac.

Warning

This project has never issued or authorized any cryptocurrency or token, and does not accept cryptocurrency payments or donations. Any cryptocurrency or token issued or promoted in this project's name, or claiming any affiliation with it, is a scam.

vphone-cli runs iOS with Apple's Virtualization.framework and PCC research virtual machines, for security research, reverse engineering, and debugging.

Documentation

Everything else lives on the documentation site: https://lakr233.github.io/vphone-cli/

  • Quick Start: requirements, host settings, and your first VM with Launchpad.
  • Manual: machines, firmware, storage, networking, and troubleshooting, in English, 中文, 日本語 and 한국어.
  • Research Notes: patches, boot chain, restore, and the automation API reference.

The sources of the site are in Documents/ and Research/.

Let an Agent Install It

If you use a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, or similar) on this Mac, paste the prompt below instead of following the steps by hand. The agent reads the vphone skill, checks what is already set up, installs Launchpad and VPhone.bundle, and stops to ask when a step needs you, such as an administrator password or a change in macOS Recovery.

Set up vphone on this Mac. Read the skill at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/main/Skills/vphone-guest-control/SKILL.md
and the files it links under references/ (same folder), then follow them:
install the newest notarized vphone-launchpad (not every release has a
-notarized zip), put vphone-launchpad-cli on PATH, install the VPhone.bundle
that matches Launchpad's series, and check `vphone-launchpad-cli status`.
Do not change SIP, boot-args or any other host security setting, and do not
create a machine until I confirm the firmware and the free disk space. When a
step needs me, tell me exactly what to do and wait.

Acknowledgements

  • wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup
  • owngoal-dev/OpenAVB and owngoal-dev/OpenSEP, the boot ROMs new VMs start from

aiSummary.oneLiner: A command-line tool for interacting with VirtualPhone, enabling automated management of virtual iOS devices.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: vphone-cli provides a terminal-based interface and automation toolkit for managing VirtualPhone instances, a platform for running virtualized iOS devices. It bridges the gap between the VirtualPhone GUI and automated CI/CD workflows by allowing developers to programmatically control device lifecycles. Users can use the CLI to create, start, stop, and snapshot virtual iPhones, as well as install applications, push files, and execute shell commands inside the virtual environment. This abstraction is critical for teams that need to integrate iOS testing, security analysis, or app deployment into headless scripts without relying on manual interaction.
keyFeatures: Device lifecycle management: Commands to boot, shutdown, and reset virtual iOS devices.
App installation: Sideload IPA files directly into the virtual environment from the command line.
File system interaction: Push and pull files between the host machine and the virtual device.
Snapshot control: Create and restore device states for reproducible testing scenarios.
Shell execution: Run commands directly within the virtual iOS environment.
CI/CD integration: Designed for headless operation within automated testing pipelines.

useCases.title: Automated iOS testing
useCases.description: QA engineers use the CLI in CI/CD pipelines to spin up a clean virtual iPhone, install a new build, and run tests.

useCases.title: Security research
useCases.description: Security analysts script the rapid deployment and teardown of specific iOS versions for vulnerability analysis.

useCases.title: App reverse engineering
useCases.description: Researchers use the tool to automate the extraction of app data and memory dumps from virtualized devices.

useCases.title: Headless device management
useCases.description: DevOps teams manage fleets of virtual iOS devices on remote servers without requiring graphical access.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This tool is built for iOS developers, QA automation engineers, and security researchers who need programmatic control over virtualized iOS environments. It requires access to VirtualPhone and familiarity with command-line interfaces.
